name: sol_token_fe_8
description: Honeypot attack via Solmate SafeTransferLib's lack of contract-existence check for ERC20 transfers
question: The source file in `source` calls Solmate's SafeTransferLib functions (safeTransfer/safeTransferFrom/safeApprove) to move ERC20 tokens without first verifying that the token address contains contract code (e.g., via extcodesize or code.length check), so a call to a non-contract or malicious token address can silently return success and enable a honeypot attack; this excludes code that uses OpenZeppelin's SafeERC20 library or that explicitly checks contract existence before the transfer.
criteria: Calls SafeTransferLib.safeTransfer(token, to, amount) directly on a user-supplied or configurable token address with no prior check that token.code.length > 0
Calls SafeTransferLib.safeTransferFrom(token, from, to, amount) without any extcodesize or contract-existence validation on token before the call
Calls SafeTransferLib.safeApprove(token, spender, amount) on an externally provided token address with no verification that the address is a deployed contract
Wraps low-level call-based transfer logic imported from Solmate's ERC20 helpers and relies solely on the call's boolean success without checking that the target has code
